breaks.claim: The figure kit's projection is left-handed while figure.md says to draw in the CAD's right-handed frame, so every figure is a mirror image of its CAD, including the shipped keypad example.
evidence: skill/sprue/kit/iso-kit.mjs:11-22: iso() sends a point to sx = x*sinA - y*cosA, and depthOf() puts the viewer at (+cosA, +sinA, +sinE)

My probe of the kit (node, grade-work/audit-sprue/tools/hand.mjs): at azimuth 45, +x goes to screen (0.89, 0.45), +y to (-0.89, 0.45), and the top face is visible (depthOf(+z) = 0.5). Seen from above, x then y turns clockwise, which is the mirror of a right-handed view. Azimuth -40 gives the same result.
skill/sprue/reference/figure.md:88-96 says to use the same frame as cad/_params.py (build123d is right-handed). It names which faces an azimuth turns toward the viewer, but nothing about mirroring.

Macropad: design.md:15-16 says 'USB end flush with the right edge'. figure.mjs:2 uses the frame 'x toward the USB end'. figure.mjs:94 sets azimuth -40, and the kit maps +x to screen (-0.81, +0.48), so down and to the LEFT.

Screen bounding boxes in examples/macropad/figure.svg (my svgbbox.py): case 'bot' x 142.6..518.0; Pico 'ctrl' x 176.3..333.2, in the left half; 'cable' x 124.5..439.3, so the cord leaves past the case's left edge. A true view from the viewer at (+x, -y) would show the USB end on the right.
The agent's workaround is co2-monitor figure.mjs:4-7, 59 (m = [x,-y,z]) and 85 (azimuth +40).
breaks.fix_idea: Make iso() right-handed: sx = -x*sinA + y*cosA, with the matching depth sign. Regenerate the macropad and ponder figures, and add a kit test that a point at +x of the CAD lands where a right-handed camera at that azimuth puts it. Until then, warn in figure.md.

breaks.claim: sprue check exits 0 when a check fails.
evidence: skill/sprue/pipeline/cli.ts:244-258 check() never sets process.exitCode, and cli.ts:481 runs `case "check": await check(); refreshPage(slug); break;`

In my copy I set design.json params.usbBudgetMa to 100. Result: '✗ The whole draw fits a USB 2.0 port ... checks: 16 run, 1 failed', then 'check exit 0'. `sprue all` also exited 0 (cli.ts:519-543 sets exitCode only for the figure).

Nothing downstream holds back either. With that failure in place, `sprue package` exited 0 (production/build-plan.md:43 says '1 failed'). `sprue accept` printed 'build accepted / every stage accepted; the package is in production/'. `sprue score` exits 0 on 'not yet' too (cli.ts:327-346).
The journal's line 'only A figure and A system fail with exit 1' is slightly off: validate (cli.ts:476), pcb, verify, faults and shot also set exit codes.
breaks.fix_idea: Set process.exitCode = 1 when checks.failed > 0 in check and all. Have package print a ✗ line for failed checks, and have accept warn on failed checks (or need --force).

breaks.claim: sprue system passes with wires, resistors and cables unplaced, and checks only the final pose.
evidence: skill/sprue/cad/system.py:463-487 placed(): a line named in `unplaced` is skipped whatever the reason given (any string passes), and a line with qtyPerUnit 0 (wire, bom.json:135-141, qtyPerBatch 1) is skipped silently, not even named.

system.py:144-151 and 644-657: Pose is used only by the stability gate (masses, pushes). Overlap, contact and clearance run once, on the as-built frame. No class or gate covers an insertion path or an assembly order.

breaks.fix_idea: Treat unplaced lines as a ⚑ flag carried to the gates, and name qtyPerBatch lines too. Allow a swept envelope for leads and cables, plus an optional Insert(part, direction, distance) that sweeps a part along its assembly path against the frame.
